about: how to request each export that attic reads. dedicated to the public domain under cc0 1.0, see guides.LICENSE.txt. text in backticks is shown as code.

guides.name: spotify
guides.wait: spotify says up to 30 days. the smaller account data often comes in about 5 days. the extended history can take longer.
steps: sign in to your spotify account on the web and open privacy settings.
under download your data, tick extended streaming history. you can tick account data too.
press request data, then confirm the request from the email spotify sends you.
when the next email arrives, download the zip. the link stops working after a while, so save the file.
guides.file: a zip such as `my_spotify_data.zip`. inside is a folder of files named like `Streaming_History_Audio_2024-2026_0.json`. drop the whole zip.
tips: account data on its own holds about a year of plays, with less detail. attic reads it, but the extended history tells a fuller story.
podcasts are kept apart from music.

guides.name: netflix
steps: sign in on the web as the account owner and open the page to download your personal information.
press submit request, then confirm it from the email netflix sends.
when the next email arrives, download the zip.
guides.file: a zip such as `netflix-report.zip`. inside is `CONTENT_INTERACTION/ViewingActivity.csv`. drop the zip or just that file.
tips: the viewing activity page has a quicker download, `NetflixViewingHistory.csv`. it holds titles and dates but no times or lengths, so attic needs the full request instead.
every profile on the account is included. attic shows each one on its own.

guides.name: youtube
guides.wait: usually minutes to a few hours. large accounts can take a day or more.
steps: open google takeout and press deselect all.
scroll down to youtube and youtube music and tick it.
press all youtube data included, press deselect all, then tick only history.
press multiple formats and set history to json. html works too, but json is more reliable.
press next step. choose to get a download link by email, export once, as a zip, then create the export.
guides.file: a takeout zip holding `Takeout/YouTube and YouTube Music/history/watch-history.json`. drop the zip. attic opens only that file, even in a big archive.
tips: watch history lists what you watched and when, not for how long, so attic counts videos, never hours.
if watch history was paused, those months will be missing.

guides.name: chatgpt
guides.wait: usually minutes, sometimes a few hours.
steps: open chatgpt, then settings, then data controls.
press export data, then confirm.
open the email and download the zip. the link stops working after about a day.
guides.file: a zip holding `conversations.json`. drop the zip.
tips: attic counts conversations, messages and words. conversation titles and your most used words are hidden in saved images unless you turn names on.

guides.name: claude
guides.wait: usually minutes to a few hours.
steps: open claude, then settings, then privacy.
press export data.
open the email and download the zip. the link stops working after a while.
guides.file: a zip holding `conversations.json`. drop the zip.
tips: conversation titles are hidden in saved images unless you turn names on.

guides.name: firefox
steps: type `about:support` in the address bar and press enter.
next to profile folder, press open folder.
quit firefox completely. while it runs, the newest visits may sit in a side file.
copy `places.sqlite` from that folder to your desktop or downloads folder.
guides.file: `places.sqlite`. drop the copy, not the original.
tips: attic reads only site names and visit times. it never reads page titles, full addresses or searches.

guides.name: chrome
steps: type `chrome://version` in the address bar and press enter.
find the profile path and open that folder in your file manager.
quit chrome completely, so the file is not locked.
copy the file named `History`, which has no extension, to your desktop or downloads folder.
guides.file: `History`. drop the copy, not the original.
tips: on a mac the folder sits inside your library, which finder hides. in finder, use go to folder and paste the profile path.
attic reads only site names and visit times. it never reads page titles, full addresses or searches.
